name: The Electron as a Rotating Bubble
description: A rotating charged oblate shell joining a flat interior to a Kerr-Newman exterior, a classical model of the spinning electron.
convention: The mass enters as $m = GM/c^2$, the signed charge length obeys $q^2 = GQ^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$, and $a = J/(Mc)$. The family has $m > 0$, $q^2 > m^2$, and $a \ge 0$. The shell lies at $r_0 = q^2/(2m)$. Tensor components apply in the smooth regions away from the shell. The Ricci tensor is $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history:
Carlos A. López enclosed a flat spacetime within a rotating charged shell in 1984 [lopez1984electron].
The exterior is the Kerr-Newman gravitational and electromagnetic field.
The boundary is an oblate ellipsoid with surface tension.
López proposed this configuration as a classical model of the spinning electron.

The shell's position follows from continuity of the geometry.
With mass length $m=GM/c^2$ and squared charge length $q^2=GQ^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$, its oblate radial coordinate is $r_0=q^2/(2m)$ [burinskii2002sources].
Its polar semiaxis is $r_0$, and its equatorial semiaxis is $\sqrt{r_0^2+a^2}$, where $a=J/(Mc)$ measures angular momentum per unit mass.
The full polar diameter $2r_0$ equals the classical electron radius when $M$ and $Q$ take the electron's mass and charge [lopez1984electron, burinskii2002sources].

The shell rotates rigidly with angular velocity $\Omega=ca/(r_0^2+a^2)$ [burinskii2002sources].
An observer at rest in the flat interior measures an equatorial speed $v=ca/\sqrt{r_0^2+a^2}$.
The speed approaches $c$ as the shell becomes more oblate.
At the electron's angular momentum $J=\hbar/2$, with $\hbar$ the reduced Planck constant, the equatorial size is close to half its reduced Compton wavelength [burinskii2016bubble].

The gravitational matching assigns the shell zero comoving energy density and finite tension in both tangential directions [burinskii2002sources].
Its tension varies with latitude.
The jump in the normal derivative of the metric fixes this surface stress, while the smooth exterior contains the electromagnetic stress.
A vanishing interior electromagnetic field and the rotating Kerr-Newman exterior require boundary structure beyond an ordinary electric surface charge and current sheet [burinskii2016bubble].
A surface dipole layer is a formal option whose electromagnetic stress needs a specified regularization.
In September 1985, Øyvind Geelmuyden Grøn reconstructed López's source through the geometry of surface layers [gron1985electron].

Static electromagnetic mass models use spherically symmetric charged matter.
The density and pressure of a charged perfect fluid can have an electromagnetic origin, with a boundary matched to the Reissner-Nordström exterior [tiwari1984mass].
Ronald Gautreau constructed static spherical electron models in 1985 by setting the matter terms to zero in the charged fluid equations [gautreau1985electron].
Grøn connected repulsive gravitation in electromagnetic mass models to negative gravitational mass and also identified repulsion in López's spinning source [gron1985repulsion].

For $m>0$ and $q^2>m^2$, the rotating bubble has no horizon.
The exterior occupies $r\ge r_0$, and a ball of flat spacetime fills the enclosed volume.
The common time coordinate has a timelike gradient throughout both regions, so it orders causal paths across the shell [lopez1984electron, burinskii2002sources].

related.text: The gravitational and electromagnetic field outside the rotating shell is Kerr-Newman's [lopez1984electron, burinskii2002sources].
Flat spacetime fills the oblate volume enclosed by the charged shell [lopez1984electron].
A charged shell separates a flat interior from an exterior electromagnetic field.

coordinates.name: Boyer-Lindquist Exterior
coordinates.convention: The common time is $t$, $r$ is the oblate radius, and $\theta$ and $\phi$ are the polar and azimuthal angles. The shell is the separate surface $r=r_0$, with polar semiaxis $r_0$ and equatorial semiaxis $\sqrt{r_0^2+a^2}$. Tensor components apply in the smooth regions away from the shell.

parameters.description: Mass length, $m = GM/c^2 > 0$, with $M$ the mass and $G$ Newton's constant
Signed charge length, $q^2 = GQ^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4) > m^2$, with $Q$ the charge and $\epsilon_0$ the vacuum permittivity
Spin length, $a = J/(Mc) \ge 0$, with $J$ the angular momentum
Oblate radius of the timelike shell

Radial function, positive throughout the retained exterior

coordinates.name: Kerr Angular Exterior
coordinates.convention: The Kerr angular time is $T$, $r$ is the oblate radius, and $\theta$ and $\psi$ are angles. The transformation from Boyer-Lindquist coordinates is $c\,dT=c\,dt+(2mr-q^2)dr/(r^2+a^2-2mr+q^2)$ and $d\psi=d\phi+a\,dr/(r^2+a^2-2mr+q^2)$ outside, with $m=q=0$ in these two transformation coefficients inside. Tensor components apply in the smooth regions away from the shell.

coordinates.name: Flat Cartesian Interior
coordinates.convention: The inertial time is $T$, and $x$, $y$, and $z$ are Cartesian lengths inside $(x^2+y^2)/(r_0^2+a^2)+z^2/r_0^2 < 1$. The angular map is $x+iy=(r+ia)e^{i\psi}\sin\theta$, $z=r\cos\theta$, with $i^2=-1$. Tensor components apply in the smooth regions away from the shell.
